pr_snapshot.body:
Residual subtraction still processed only eight columns per SIMD iteration and paid repeated slice/row setup. Add bounded 16-column kernels copied/adapted from goav1, with exact-width 4/8-column paths and conservative alias/short-window fallback. No new dependency or handwritten assembly.

On Apple M4 Max with Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six balanced native runs retain all 48 public component wins: **1.71–3.02× faster than the immediate parent**, with every paired sample at least 1.65× and zero allocations. Larger contiguous kernels also beat the old NEON path; padded-output old-reference cases select scalar fallback and are reported separately.

Whole-codec ARM VP9 improves **1.34% at 320×180 and 2.98% at 720p** versus the parent, all six pairs faster. It still takes 8.84%/35.22% more time than old assembly. The VP8 control is +0.49% with mixed pairs; residual subtraction has no VP8 production caller. These component wins remain useful independently of whole-codec results. Exact-head native x64 and optimized-libvpx results are complete below; Rosetta checks establish correctness only.

Full suite, ARM race/checkptr, AMD checkptr and actual AVX-off fallback pass. Differential coverage includes 5,760 geometries, read-only aliases, overlapping outputs, minimum windows, extreme/unused strides, and full post-panic state. PGO/fingerprint, noasm, SIMD selection and pre-commit gates pass. The native harness preserves all 282 existing cases and adds 48 identical public fixtures to both references; no correctness gate is relaxed.

Raw samples, sources, diagnostics, all outliers and reproducible scope are in `benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-arm64/2026-10-18-residual-rows/REPORT.md` and its hashed archives. README files are untouched.

Based on merged #37 and #38. The latter’s native x64 audit retains its +0.88% whole-VP8 regression alongside 27/36 new SSE cases exceeding 1.5× in every sample; the full results and allocation outlier are preserved in the baseline archives. The rebase onto latest main preserved the complete successor tree, and all six locally measured source hashes still match.

Final exact-head `968b518b` evidence (Go1.27.2, PGOoff):

- On **EPYC 9V45**, all **48 changed subtraction fixtures improve versus the parent SIMD in every pair**: median **1.939–6.626×**, minimum paired gain **1.771×**. All 288 pairs exceed 1.5×. Old-reference ratios **1.697–19.379×** are versus **SCALAR fallback for all48 AMD cases**, because the pinned AMD fast selector always declines; they do not measure active x64 assembly. ARM contiguous-output NEON and padded scalar-reference results remain separately scoped.
- All **330 kernels × six samples × three variants** report zero bytes/allocations. Fourteen source hashes match, **123 targeted checks / 268 PASS lines** include all new subtraction tests under selected SIMD and race/checkptr, and no required test fails/skips. All22 semantic fields match across public/profile outputs. Preserve the **old-reference VP9 720 round4 allocation outlier 1.266667 versus modal1.25**; all current, parent and profile samples match their controls.
- Whole VP9 320 is **+0.4638% time versus parent** (3/6 pairs faster), while VP9 720 improves **−2.5042%** (5/6). They remain **−45.4753% / −52.8351% versus the old reference build** on this CPU. **VP8 is an unchanged-source control: +3.5742% versus parent** (1/6 faster), **+1.8878% versus the old build**. No VP8 algorithm benefit, universal x64 win or cross-CPU gap-closure claim.
- Keep **all167 median regressions and eight all-six-slower subpixel controls**, ranging +1.797–6.034%, with every raw pair. Subtraction itself has no regressing fixture. Short VP9 profiles sample the new bounded/16-row path; sampled times are not additive causal estimates.
- Optimized C is separately measured on **EPYC 7763**. Fixed-speed VP8 Go takes **2.362811× libvpx time** (+136.2811%; libvpx is faster), matching measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/frame counts without proving bitstream identity. This is a VP8 control for this change. Adaptive VP8 +77.6720% and VP9 +190.5841%/+200.7965% compare unequal quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches timed outputs in this job. All reference timers use `vpxenc-stats`; pinned ASM/SSE2/AVX2/runtime dispatch are enabled. Native/C hosts and different source checkpoints are never combined into a causal speed claim.

All three exact-head checks pass. Complete native86/C74 raw logs, audit, independent source/hash proof, output/allocation exceptions and report are preserved for the successor archive. README files remain unchanged.

+//go:build goexperiment.simd && amd64 && !purego
+
+package pixel
+
+import (
+	"simd/archsimd"
+	"unsafe"
+)
+
+func subtract16Rows(sp unsafe.Pointer, ss int, pp unsafe.Pointer, ps int, op unsafe.Pointer, os, w, h int) bool {
+	defer archsimd.ClearAVXUpperBits()
+	var bits archsimd.Int16x16
+	for {
+		for x := 0; x < w; x += 16 {
+			a := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, x)))
+			b := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(pp, x)))
+			d := a.ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16().Sub(b.ExtendToUint16().BitsToInt16())
+			d.StoreArray((*[16]int16)(unsafe.Add(op, 2*x)))
+			bits = bits.Or(d)
+		}
+		h--
+		if h == 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		// Advance only when another row remains; each pointer stays within
+		// its validated object even with an unused large final stride.
+		sp = unsafe.Add(sp, ss)
+		pp = unsafe.Add(pp, ps)
+		op = unsafe.Add(op, 2*os)
+	}
+	q := bits.GetLo().Or(bits.GetHi()).ToBits().ReshapeToUint64s()
+	return q.GetElem(0)|q.GetElem(1) != 0
+}

+//go:build goexperiment.simd && arm64 && !purego

+func subtract16Rows(sp unsafe.Pointer, ss int, pp unsafe.Pointer, ps int, op unsafe.Pointer, os, w, h int) bool {
+	var bits archsimd.Int16x8
+	for {
+		for x := 0; x < w; x += 16 {
+			a := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(sp, x)))
+			b := archsimd.LoadUint8x16Array((*[16]byte)(unsafe.Add(pp, x)))
+			lo := widen8(a).Sub(widen8(b))
+			hi := widenHi8(a).BitsToInt16().Sub(widenHi8(b).BitsToInt16())

+			hi.StoreArray((*[8]int16)(unsafe.Add(op, 2*(x+8))))
+			bits = bits.Or(lo).Or(hi)
+		}
+		h--
+		if h == 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		// Advance only when another row remains; each pointer stays within
+		// its validated object even with an unused large final stride.
+		sp = unsafe.Add(sp, ss)
+		pp = unsafe.Add(pp, ps)
+		op = unsafe.Add(op, 2*os)
+	}
+	q := bits.ToBits().ReshapeToUint64s()
+	return q.GetElem(0)|q.GetElem(1) != 0
+}
diff --git a/internal/pixel/subtract_rows_simd.go b/internal/pixel/subtract_rows_simd.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..84b3a558
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/pixel/subtract_rows_simd.go
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+//go:build goexperiment.simd && (arm64 || amd64) && !purego
+
+package pixel
+
+import (
+	"simd/archsimd"
+	"unsafe"
+)
+
+// The caller bounds dimensions and strides. Decline incomplete windows so
+// the checked fallback preserves its original partial-write/panic behavior.
+func subtractRowsBounded(src []byte, ss int, pred []byte, ps int, out []int16, os, w, h int) (bool, bool) {
+	sn, pn, on := (h-1)*ss+w, (h-1)*ps+w, (h-1)*os+w
+	if sn > len(src) || pn > len(pred) || on > len(out) {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	sp, pp, op := unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(src)), unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(pred)), unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(out))
+	// Wider reads must not observe output stores earlier than the eight-lane
+	// fallback. Read-only input aliases are fine; output/input overlap declines.
+	su, pu, ou := uintptr(sp), uintptr(pp), uintptr(op)
+	if ou-su < uintptr(sn) || su-ou < uintptr(2*on) || ou-pu < uintptr(pn) || pu-ou < uintptr(2*on) {
+		return false, false
+	}
+	if w == 4 {
+		return subtractSmallRows4(sp, ss, pp, ps, op, os, h), true
+	}
+	if w == 8 {
+		return subtractSmallRows8(sp, ss, pp, ps, op, os, h), true
+	}
+	return subtract16Rows(sp, ss, pp, ps, op, os, w, h), true
+}
+
+func subtractSmallRows4(sp unsafe.Pointer, ss int, pp unsafe.Pointer, ps int, op unsafe.Pointer, os, h int) bool {
+	var bits archsimd.Int16x8
+	for {
+		a := (archsimd.Uint32x4{}).SetElem(0, *(*uint32)(sp)).ReshapeToUint8s()
+		b := (archsimd.Uint32x4{}).SetElem(0, *(*uint32)(pp)).ReshapeToUint8s()
+		d := widen8(a).Sub(widen8(b))
+		*(*uint64)(op) = d.ToBits().ReshapeToUint64s().GetElem(0)
+		bits = bits.Or(d)
+		h--
+		if h == 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		sp = unsafe.Add(sp, ss)
+		pp = unsafe.Add(pp, ps)
+		op = unsafe.Add(op, 2*os)
+	}
+	q := bits.ToBits().ReshapeToUint64s()
+	return q.GetElem(0)|q.GetElem(1) != 0
+}
+
+func subtractSmallRows8(sp unsafe.Pointer, ss int, pp unsafe.Pointer, ps int, op unsafe.Pointer, os, h int) bool {
+	var bits archsimd.Int16x8
+	for {
+		a := (archsimd.Uint64x2{}).SetElem(0, *(*uint64)(sp)).ReshapeToUint8s()
+		b := (archsimd.Uint64x2{}).SetElem(0, *(*uint64)(pp)).ReshapeToUint8s()
+		d := widen8(a).Sub(widen8(b))
+		d.StoreArray((*[8]int16)(op))
+		bits = bits.Or(d)
+		h--
+		if h == 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		sp = unsafe.Add(sp, ss)
+		pp = unsafe.Add(pp, ps)
+		op = unsafe.Add(op, 2*os)
+	}
+	q := bits.ToBits().ReshapeToUint64s()
+	return q.GetElem(0)|q.GetElem(1) != 0
+}

# Bounded SIMD residual subtraction

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 darwin/arm64 archsimd, PGO off, GOMAXPROCS=1.
Immediate parent 6a7b1444765e30fcbcc4a5aca8abd1af73dd9013 includes the repaired
AMD vertical carrier from PR #37 and the SSE winner from PR #38. Old assembly
reference 691cd0512c4829d9ee40d483205dd223f9eb028d. No cross-CPU attribution.

Adapt the sixteen-column residual layout from goav1 residualBlockSIMD at
0f40b2bd848d8c5c7bdbaa016f2ced3085f7fc7a, with no module dependency. ARM loads
16 pixels and stores two eight-coefficient packets. AMD widens to AVX2, stores
16 coefficients and defers upper-state cleanup. Dedicated four/eight-pixel
kernels read exactly 4/8 bytes, compute signed int16 residuals and store exactly
4/8 coefficients. Four-pixel unused SIMD lanes remain zero. Fused OR over all
computed residuals preserves nonzero even if later output rows overlap earlier.

The dispatcher proves widths 4/8 or 16-multiples through 64, h=1..64 and nonnegative
strides<2^30. Complete visible input/output lengths are checked before unsafe
access. Their row offsets fit below 2^36, output byte offsets below 2^37. Typed
row pointers advance only when another row remains, never forming an unused
out-of-object final pointer. Zero/overlapping strides and read-only input
aliases remain valid; output/input overlap conservatively declines BEFORE
stores, preserving the original eight-lane/scalar partial-write ordering.
Short windows decline to the original checked fallback, preserving its panic
and whole-buffer post-panic state. Larger/unsupported geometry and CPU-off keep
the parent behavior. No handwritten assembly, production cgo or new dependency.

Fresh six balanced parent/assembly/current orders, 100ms per 48 identical public
B.Loop fixtures: eight shapes, two stride/output layouts and random/max-error/
identical patterns. Origins 3/5 and coefficient origin 1, exact visible windows,
independent per-coefficient and boolean oracles before/after timing, complete
input and output backing canaries, and observable outputs. Every kernel sample
has zero B/op and allocations. Ranges cover the three pixel patterns.
